dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: yasya kasyāpi varṇasya pūrvāntāv anubhāvayet | śūnyayā śūnyabhūto 'sau śūnyākāraḥ pumān bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Whoever dwells in the silence before any sound-syllable (varṇa) begins and after it ends becomes, through the power of that void, void himself: his very form becomes open space.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: contemplate the condition of a letter before it is uttered and after it is uttered as mere void; 'the power of the void' is parāśakti, and 'becoming the form of the void' means no longer identifying with the breath-body as the Self. Wallis reads 'the beginning and/or ending of any syllable whatsoever'. Singh classes it as śāktopāya ending in śāmbhavopāya.
dharana.technique_name: The Silence Before and After a Sound
dharana.instruction: Say one soft syllable and rest in the silence just before and just after it.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 40 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a line in time: silence, then one syllable, then silence. Attention rests on the two silences that frame the sound.
geometry.svg_hint: a short sound-wave drawn in the middle of a long empty line, with the empty stretches on both sides highlighted
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Frame the sound
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the sound is felt as a brief shape inside a larger silence that was there before it and remains after it. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: the silence after the syllable fades
breath.cue: Natural breath. On some out-breaths, say one soft syllable such as 'ma'; let it end with the breath. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn toward the edges of the sound: just before it starts and just after it stops
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The silence immediately before and immediately after a single syllable

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Whoever dwells in the silence before any sound-syllable (varṇa) begins and after it ends becomes, through the power of that void, void himself: his very form becomes open space.
adiyogi.method_summary: Say a single syllable softly, or hear one. Before it, rest in the silence it will come out of; after it, stay in the silence it goes back into. Let the syllable be small and the silences large. No straining to hear.

honesty.disclosure: Door 017 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 17 (verse 40) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 017 is dharana 17, verse 40. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).

The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Keep any voiced syllable soft; there is no need to project the voice. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 017: the silence before and after a sound. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 17, verse 40.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie down in any easy way. The map is a line: silence, one syllable, silence.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Say one soft syllable, or listen for one. Rest in the silence before it, and stay in the silence after it.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a small sound inside a large silence. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 40: dwell on what comes before and after any syllable, and through the power of the void one becomes open space. Let the sound be small and the silence large.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.
